survey: An upright hexagonal wooden coffin stands on grass, turned three-quarters to the camera. The lid faces the viewer and carries a raised wooden cross, which sits flat on the lid and is attached properly. On the right, the side of the box shows, and it follows the same six-sided outline. Between the lid's right edge and the box side there is a long, even vertical gap running the full height, filled with purple padded lining. Across the top, one flat cap covers both the lid and the box, with only a faint seam between them. The bottom rests on the grass with tufts around the base, and its contact shadow looks right.

errors.where: Right edge of the lid, along the full height
errors.what: The lid does not close onto the box, and it has not swung open on a hinge either. It is shifted sideways as one flat slab, leaving an even gap filled with bulging purple lining. The lining sits where the box's side wall and the lid edge should meet. Nothing holds the lid in this position (no hinge, and no box wall on the left to match), so the lid and box do not add up to a container that could close.

The top of the lid and the top of the box blend into one continuous cap, while lower down the lid and side are separate parts with a gap between them. The part that should be separate at the top is fused, so the lid could not open.

fix: Upright hexagonal wooden coffin with the lid closed flush on the front of the box. The lid's edges meet the box's side walls all the way around, with only a thin seam and no gap or visible lining. Box side walls of even thickness on both sides. The lid's top edge is clearly separate from the box's top end panel. Raised wooden cross centered on the lid.
